clue.text: Threats can seem ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests absurd disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off threats that sound absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Menaces and threats are synonyms, both meaning warnings of harm to come.

clue.text: Chain letters?

definitions.meaning: armour of linked metal rings, as in chain armour
the post that arrives each day

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both linked-ring armour (chain armour) and the post delivered to a house.

clue.text: Refusal to start on time

indicators.note: the refusal comes at the start, before the other word

parts.note: no is a refusal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to begin punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular time of day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Oarsman overturned in vessel in distress

indicators.note: the turned oarsman goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

indicators.note: overturned means the oarsman's word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A rower capsizes and ends up struggling in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat to go with the oarsman, but it is a tin; 'overturned' reverses the rower and 'in' puts him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn describes someone worn down by worry, i.e. showing signs of distress.

clue.text: Only about five find the answer

indicators.note: about means the word for only goes around the numeral

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Only around five people manage to work out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to find its answer.

clue.text: One group, about six, backing pleasure gardens

indicators.note: backing means the whole assembled run is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means the group word goes around the numeral for six

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A party of people, around six of them, heads back to a park.
explanation.walkthrough: I + LO(VI)T gives ILOVIT, and 'backing' turns it round. The Tivoli Gardens in Copenhagen are the famous pleasure gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Tivoli is the name of famous pleasure gardens in Copenhagen, and a generic term for such amusement grounds.

clue.text: Naughty ladies men dream of

definitions.note: the definition stands for the things men dream of, a noun phrase

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Men fantasise about naughty women.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect visions that people aspire to and dream about.

clue.text: They are extensively used by oarsmen

definitions.text: They are extensively used by oarsmen

parts.words: They are extensively used by oarsmen
parts.note: extensively suggests heavy use, but means things that extend out from a boat's side to hold the rowlocks

explanation.definitionFit: Rowing boats have projecting frames on their sides that carry the rowlocks beyond the hull.

clue.text: Cow I'd give information about

indicators.note: about means the word for giving information goes around the contraction

parts.note: to intimate is to make known or hint
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone about to pass on information regarding a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Club regulation that must be strictly obeyed

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A society's bylaw that members must strictly follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: a regulation that must be strictly obeyed is the sense of the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid, unbending regulation is called an iron one, enforced without exception.

clue.text: Set of six texts distributed around the East

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the abbreviation
distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A batch of messages is sent out to six recipients in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges TEXTS to SEXTT, and 'around' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, most often musicians.

clue.text: Double up, for example, in pain

parts.note: a twin is a double or exact counterpart

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone doubles over in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EG into GE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pain.

clue.text: Tender bill for plant?

parts.note: sweet means tender or gentle
Bill is a short form of the name William

explanation.surface: An invoice for a plant, offered gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an account, but it is the man's name Bill, short for William.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a garden plant of the pink family with clustered flowers.

clue.text: The potato's dug out — a tuber?

indicators.note: dug out suggests digging the soil, so the letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its s included as a letter

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts a potato, wondering whether it is a tuber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tuber?' is a pun: not a root vegetable but something that comes in a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste is sold squeezed from a tube, so it is jokingly a tube-dweller.

clue.text: Being thrown together, German joined the Italian in bar

parts.note: Jerry is an old slang term for a German

indicators.note: the Italian article goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: During a building boom, a German teamed up with an Italian in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means except, giving BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry-built means cheaply and hastily constructed, slapped together.

clue.text: Main reason for horse being tired?

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, as in the main concern
a horse ridden too much would be exhausted

explanation.definitionFit: The word means paramount or principal, and can be read as excessive riding that tires a horse.

clue.text: Ridicule made clear in a letter

indicators.note: the word for clear goes inside the spelt-out letter

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
to rid is to clear, as in rid the house of mice

explanation.surface: Mockery spelt out plainly in a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule.

clue.text: A deity to follow in retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A god to whom one remains devoted after leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A god is a deity, a divine being.

clue.text: A pupil originally with little desire to take courses

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word for a student

parts.note: petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A student with little enthusiasm for enrolling in classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' looks like classes for the pupil, but means the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the desire to eat, i.e. to work through a meal's courses.

clue.text: Salt used as a preservative

definitions.meaning: an old salt is an experienced sailor
a black substance used to protect wood and rope

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a sailor and names the pitch-like substance used to protect timber.

clue.text: Drinks on the house for independent type

definitions.meaning: complimentary liquor, read as no-charge alcohol
a person who lives without conventional constraints

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a nonconformist person and can be read as liquor given at no charge.

clue.text: Coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: a sheep's woolly coat, or a warm jacket

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a woolly coat and, as a verb, to cheat someone of money.

clue.text: Plastered and stoned

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a wall rendered with plaster and finished with embedded small stones.

clue.text: Polite American rises to welcome

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
ave is a Latin greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: A courteous American stands up to greet someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns US into SU in this down entry; AVE is Latin for hail.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smoothly polite and charming.

clue.text: Hoax article used as a tailpiece

parts.note: cod as an adjective means fake or a hoax
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fake piece of writing is tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a concluding passage, a tailpiece to a work.

clue.text: Become engaged in some sharp practice

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in a bit of underhand dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when they become engaged with one another.

clue.text: Running shoes have these laces

definitions.meaning: metal points on the soles of athletics shoes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names sprinters' sole points and, as a verb, adding strong drink to something.

clue.text: A singer can measure one wrong note

parts.note: a bar is a measure of music
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the word are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A vocalist manages to hit one wrong note.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer with a voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Good reputation to consider

definitions.meaning: high regard in which someone is held

explanation.definitionFit: The word means high regard as a noun and to regard or deem as a verb.

clue.text: Asian trees? Nonsense!

parts.note: E stands for Eastern, hence Asian
the yew is a tree
the ash is also a tree

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses talk of trees in Asia as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for humbug or rubbish talk.
